instructions: Replace /replace-me/ with a regex that matches a whole identifier: it starts with a letter, followed by zero or more letters or digits. The five console.log lines are already written. Leave them alone and change only the regex, until the console prints true, true, false, false, false — one per line.
starter:
// Rule: a letter, then any letters or digits.
const identifier = /replace-me/;

console.log(identifier.test("count1")); // true
console.log(identifier.test("x"));      // true
console.log(identifier.test("1count")); // false
console.log(identifier.test("my-var")); // false
console.log(identifier.test(""));       // false
hints: `^` pins the match to the start of the string and `$` pins it to the end. Without both, `my-var` passes because it *contains* `my`.
The first character is exactly one letter: `[a-zA-Z]`. Everything after it is `[a-zA-Z0-9]` repeated zero or more times — that's what `*` means.

tests.description: "count1" matches — letter first, digits allowed after
"x" matches — one letter is a whole identifier
"1count" is rejected — can't start with a digit
"my-var" is rejected — the regex is anchored at both ends
The empty string is rejected — there must be a first letter
